title: Making 'Tuxedo Junction' and the band's sound
summary: He finished the tune in the 1939 Victor session, named it at his valet's suggestion, and built the band's sound around that tempo.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When did you first get a sound that had gelled and you said that's the sound that we will want for the band? How did that come into being?
Well, I can say about the time when we was recording, like we did things like "Tuxedo Junction". Well, that was, we made that in 1939. We actually finished that
tune in the studio. I took, Bill Johnson and Julian Dash were co-writers. They used to play the first 8 bars as a theme to bring the next band onto the stand. And, that's about all we got of that.
You were in the process of giving us some idea of how you actually got the sound that you wanted for the band and how you pursued that.
Oh, I think I was talking about "Tuxedo Junction".

Well, when we went to record a session, that was in 1939. We went down to [RCA] Victor.* The tune was finished there. They wanted to know what my sixth tune was gonna be. I said give me a half hour. So, I took my rhythm section and I went over to a corner and I made up the introduction and finished out the first chorus. And then, I got back to the band. We talked over an ensemble chorus for the last chorus because the music in the beginning wasn't even on paper. We did that from head. We finished the whole tune. Once we finished the tune there, then I liked that beat and that sound. After that, then we named the tune after the tape was made. My valet at the time was Roy
* RCA Victor did not exist then; it was merely Victor Records.

Mack, and he said Hawk, why don't you call it "Tuxedo Junction" cause I was asking for suggestions as to what we should call it. Then, he said you used to play out there all the time in the summer. He said call it "Tuxedo Junction". So, I said that's it.

And so, that tune from that beat kind of stuck with me, and that tempo. And, I liked that. So, we started talking other arrangements over and tried to stay somewhere near that. And, that's how we actually, it kind of got to me then. And, I liked that tempo, although we did other things. But, that tempo and that sound.

Sam, he did a lot of writing by putting certain things around me when I went up to the high section. He built it around that way. And we liked that. We did some tunes that way on the recordings and I liked it. We just stuck with that formula.
